text:
Maria G: Quick coord — I'm opening a tiny PR to clarify tenant-affinity effects on autoscale cooldowns. we have a few customers confused: they expect cooldown to pause while a tenant is draining but in our runtime it still counts. can we put a short explainer + a YAML example that shows 'hold_for: tenant-drain' and a python SDK snippet that demonstrates how to opt into 'graceful_scale'?

Jonah K: yeah this bit tripped me up when onboarding. short FAQ blurb + example yaml SGTM. do we have to change SLA wording? seems like 'best-effort' is safer than implying pause.

Shiv P: pinging eng-runtime and eng-platform for accuracy @Jonah K @Maria G — runtime does not currently suspend cooldown timers; we added a flag 'graceful_scale:true' last quarter but it's opt-in and only for dedicated pools. i'll confirm exact behavior.

Eli S: small nit: customers read samples first, so prefer a tiny runnable snippet. e.g. show a scalePolicy fragment and a 3-line python call.

Maria G: good call. i'll draft the YAML and python, leave wording conservative. putting a TODO: link to the ticket about making cooldown pausable in future.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5123 — branch: docs/tenant-affinity-cooldown-clarify 

Jonah K: nice. can someone add an inline comment that mentions effect on SLA (latency SLO unaffected; capacity SLA still counts time during drain)? we should avoid 'pause SLA' phrasing.

Shiv P: confirmed with runtime: 'graceful_scale:true' delays preemption of warm instances until KV cache is flushed, but the autoscale cooldown timer keeps running. so the doc should say: "cooldown continues; graceful_scale reduces waste but does not extend cooldown".

Maria G: drafting now. sample YAML (for the docs):
```yaml
scalePolicy:
  kind: cooldown-aware
  cooldown: 300s
  graceful_scale: true  # opt-in: avoids unnecessary preemption during tenant drain
  hold_for: tenant-drain
```

Maria G: python SDK snippet (short):
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
policy = {
    "cooldown": 300,
    "graceful_scale": True,
}
client.update_scale_policy(pool_id, policy)
```

Eli S: perfect. can we also include a CLI one-liner? most customers copy-paste that.

Maria G: adding a CLI example: `rwctl pool patch --id $POOL --set scalePolicy.graceful_scale=true --set scalePolicy.cooldown=300`

Jonah K: wording suggestion for the FAQ line: "Note: cooldown timers continue to run during tenant draining; enabling graceful_scale reduces preemption but does not extend the cooldown window." short and clear.

Shiv P: +1. also adding a cross-ref to the Dedicated SLA doc section on capacity commitments. i'll leave an inline review on the PR for the exact phrasing.

Maria G: thanks — i'll push edits. action items: (1) me: update PR with YAML/py/cli + FAQ blurb, (2) Shiv: confirm runtime wording in review, (3) Jonah: check SLA cross-ref line, (4) Eli: add one-liner to examples index. aim to merge by EOD.

docs-bot: CI passed for PR #5123 — lint ok, link-checker flagged one relative link (docs/dedicated/sla.md#capacity) as 404 (needs update).

Maria G: thanks bot — i'll fix the link to point to /docs/dedicated/sla/commitments.md and update the PR.

Jonah K: if we need a followup, let's create a short "behavior matrix" in the handbook showing combinations of {graceful_scale, cooldown, hold_for} and outcomes. might help support calls.

Maria G: agree. leaving a followup card after merge. merging now when checks are green. :shipit:

docs-bot: PR merged (5123) by Maria G — changes deployed to staging docs site.

Eli S: awesome. can someone paste the final link here once staging is live? i'll add to the onboarding checklist.

Maria G: staging: https://staging.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/tenant-affinity-cooldown.html — please verify and i'll promote to prod tomorrow.

Shiv P: looked quick — wording looks accurate from runtime side. left one tiny grammar nit.

Jonah K: verified example behaviour with a local sim, matches doc. good to promote.

Maria G: thanks everyone — closing thread.
